p7_b0.ocr: In the study of DAMP, various disease models illustrate the effects of deletion. For Biglycan, renal inflammation (unilateral ureteral obstruction) showed reduced kidney damage, as referenced in [87]. In the sepsis model using LPS or zymosan, deletion provided protection from lethality, referenced in [23, 87]. FNEDA demonstrated reduced lesion size, number, and macrophage infiltration in atherosclerosis (Apo E deficient, high fat diet), as noted in [139].

p7_b1.ocr: MRP8/MRP14 indicated reduced bacterial dissemination, systemic inflammation, and liver damage during abdominal sepsis (E. coli), with reference [140]. Furthermore, arterial injury (femoral wire insertion) revealed reduced inflammatory cell infiltration and neointimal formation, referenced in [141]. Atherosclerosis (Apo E deficient, high fat diet) was also associated with attenuated atherosclerotic lesions and macrophage accumulation in plaques, as mentioned in [141].

Lethal sepsis (LPS) provided evidence that deletion protects from lethality, referenced in [143].
